target: Observed mammal diel activity reallocation between rising/falling photoperiod branches at equal daylength, tested for cross-landscape transfer
epistemic_note: Publication/landing-page design evidence is NOT verification of original event rows or physical camera-hour operation. None of these candidates currently qualifies as an independent source-verified Tier-A positive branch effect.

sources.reference: Kays et al. (2020) Methods in Ecology and Evolution, DOI 10.1111/2041-210X.13370
sources.region_notes: Montana and North Carolina: temperature seasons; China, Peru, Panama: precipitation seasons. Panama cameras relocated every 7–12 days within 10 survey blocks; Peru monthly effort unequal.
sources.time_coverage_evidence: At least one continuous calendar year for seasonal subsets described in Methods, with Panama rotation exception
sources.candidate_value: Highest-priority independent multi-biome audit; original seasonal.zip member schema must be inspected before claiming five Tier-A replicates.
sources.source_access_status_20261015: API metadata successfully retrieved including SHA256; binary download returned HTTP 401 in independent public-page reader, CI receipt HOLD; no raw rows read

sources.reference: Jeon and Lim (2026) Biodiversity Data Journal 14:e191556
sources.time_coverage_evidence: April 2022–May 2023 (published); the frozen 41 original equal-daylength pairs have no authenticated raw event/operation input
sources.candidate_value: Frozen original 41 date-pair design; independent source integrity and user-completed official usage declaration required; #265.

sources.reference: Rhode Island 2018–2023 public v3; exploratory ODSP PRs #225, #228, #229
sources.time_coverage_evidence: Winter and summer campaigns 2018–2023; do not infer repeated same-daylength rising/falling within-site support
sources.candidate_value: Observed comparative scoring shows seasonal information matters but different clock/solar model output geometry prevents biological clock attribution.

sources.reference: Swanson et al. (2015) Scientific Data; Snapshot Serengeti
sources.time_coverage_evidence: Multi-year savanna camera monitoring; EXIF first/last valid images on each SD card define published start/end dates
sources.candidate_value: Potential environmental season test near equator; first/last EXIF-valid capture dates are not independently measured hardware on-hours.

source_date_only_replay_20261015.source_definition: first/last valid SD card photo date intervals; calendar/geometry proxy only, not actual station×hour hardware ON/OFF

sources.reference: Moesch et al. (2026) Dryad Freiburg urban mammal camera data
sources.time_coverage_evidence: Published timestamp, season and season-year per detection; publication states continuous cameras but source also only documents MaxDays sampling metric
sources.candidate_value: Independent European region and urban gradient; verify yearlong detection/deployment support by camera before matched-daylength design.

sources.reference: Snapshot USA 2019–2023 data; Snapshot USA 2024 DOI 10.5061/dryad.bnzs7h4qf
sources.candidate_value: Broad spatial/latitude test for falling branch only, not an annual-loop hysteresis replicate.

sources.reference: Fukasawa et al. (2025) Biodiversity Data Journal 13:e141168
sources.candidate_value: Standardized Japanese autumn comparator; no same-year rising branch.

sources.reference: McMurry (2026) NEON subprojects + four US forests
sources.time_coverage_evidence: Source explicitly says EACH subproject sampled once for about one month in early growing season, despite multi-year pooled calendar dates
sources.candidate_value: Independent spatial survey, not repeat rising-vs-falling seasons.

sources.time_coverage_evidence: June 2012–June 2014 two-year study; paper states all relevant data within paper, no separately verified individual event table
sources.candidate_value: Prior species-specific seasonal peak shifts; cannot be relabeled as novel or an independently re-computed same-daylength result.

sources.reference: Hebblewhite et al. (2020) Movebank Data Repository; Ya Ha Tinda female elk 2001–2020
sources.time_coverage_evidence: Multiyear GPS trajectories; variable collar duty cycles, including ~1 fix/13 h in a later phase, preclude treating GPS fixes as equal-hour activity rates
sources.candidate_value: Independent sensor-type triangulation candidate, but not direct equivalence to camera activity or automatically valid diel sampling.

last_source_audit: 2026-10-15: official Dryad Kays file SHA256; true source-only 225-station Serengeti mirror-date overlap 186 sites, 25,016 candidate site-date pairs.
